what_happened: Research confirmed the Write-tool path already resolves markers whole-file correctly today (tool_input.content IS the full new file); only the Edit path has the snippet-only defect. This narrowed the fix to one path plus a depth-counter upgrade in the shared library, and let the Write-side test cases be framed as regression guards rather than new feature work.

Planning discovered that the research report's recommended depth-counter + validity tightening of strip_exempt_regions is NOT behavior-preserving on the current tree: five source-store test files (test-check-task-references.sh, test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh, test-git-commit-phase.sh, test-git-commit-scoped.sh, test-orchestrate-record-decision.sh) end their marker parse at eof_depth>0, partly from redundant nested begins and partly because PROSE that merely mentions the literal token is itself parsed as a marker. Under the new rule those files' trailing regions become scannable and the repo-wide lint would go red. The plan therefore adds a marker-hygiene remediation phase ahead of the library change, which the research report did not anticipate.

A single awk depth-trace one-liner over git ls-files pinpointed every imbalanced marker file and its first unclosed begin line in one pass, converting an unbounded 'which files might break' worry into a closed five-file list with exact line numbers before any code was written. The same one-liner is reusable as the plan's own verification command and as the basis for the new library balance-report function.

test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh's cold-baseline/gate10 cases failed (30s timeout exceeded) during Phase 1 re-verification; this matches the pre-existing documented known-failures.txt row (load-sensitive gate10/specs-state.json-size) and is unrelated to this task's marker-hygiene edit -- the task-reference lint and Case G4 assertions in the same run both PASSED.
git-commit-scoped.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json' from a commit pathspec: not contained in task #443's declared file_scope.

generate-context-line-counts.sh --write (run to fix MY OWN task-reference-exemptions.md line_count drift after my Phase 4 doc edit) also found the shell-script-testing.md entry already correct at 899 in the on-disk index-entries.json -- a pre-existing, uncommitted, out-of-task-443-scope change already present in the working tree at dispatch start (per the session's initial git status snapshot), presumably a concurrent sibling task's own pending fix for its own edit to that file. Committing index-entries.json via git-commit-scoped.sh (a whole-file commit, since that script re-reads the working tree fresh for the named pathspec) unavoidably swept that sibling's already-correct content into my own task-443-attributed commit (41dca751a). The CONTENT is correct either way (899 matches actual current line count); only the commit attribution is off -- the sibling's own fix landed under my commit message instead of theirs. No revert was made: reverting would regress a correct value back to stale (827), which is strictly worse. Reported per Stage 3.6 Observation Duty rather than silently dismissed.

Phase 5's post-redeploy gate-4 re-run found a REAL finding (not load-sensitive timeout noise): test-validate-no-task-references.sh's own header prose (pre-existing, not authored by this task) contained a same-line 'both substrings' prose mention (line 22: both :begin and :end on one line) plus a separate :end-only prose mention (line 25). Every ad-hoc whole-tree balance-trace snippet used throughout Phases 1-4 of this implementation (copied verbatim from the plan text) checks /task-ref-ok:begin/ before /task-ref-ok:end/ per-line, so a same-line-both-tokens line is misclassified as a pure begin -- exactly mirroring the OLD boolean toggle's own quirk. The REAL shared library's new parser (this task's own Phase 2 deliverable) deliberately classifies a same-line-both line as a net-zero no-op instead, which correctly exposed the previously-invisible stray end from line 25. Caught only because Phase 5 ran the ACTUAL deployed library via gate 4, not an ad-hoc trace. Fixed by rewording the prose (no longer embeds the literal substrings) and reconfirmed clean via a direct marker_balance_report sweep of the whole tree (not the naive ad-hoc awk snippet).

Discovered (not caused by this task) while exercising the deployed test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh directly during Phase 5 verification: its REPO_ROOT computation (scripts/tests/test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh line 75, REPO_ROOT=$(cd "$CORE_DIR/../../.." && pwd)) is calibrated for the source-store path depth (core/scripts -> 3 '..' lands at agent-system/, still inside the real repo, so it works by accident) but is off-by-one for the deployed path depth (.claude/scripts -> 3 '..' lands at the PARENT of the repo root, e.g. /home/benjamin/.config instead of /home/benjamin/.config/nvim). Running the DEPLOYED copy directly therefore fails its own git-worktree-fixture setup step with 'fatal: not a git repository' (suppressed by the script's own >/dev/null 2>&1, surfacing only as 'ERROR: could not create a git worktree fixture'). The SOURCE-STORE invocation is unaffected and was re-confirmed green (15 passed, 2 failed -- the same pre-existing documented gate10/gate4 load-sensitive timeout pair, not a worktree failure). Out of this task's own scope (443 is about the task-reference hook, not this script's path arithmetic) and the plan's Phase 5 explicitly modifies no source files; left unfixed and reported for a future owner.
